observations: Debtor days have increased to 42.58 in the latest management accounts (2025-09-08) from 30.21 in FY2024.
Creditor days show a sharp decline in 2025, suggesting either a change in supplier payment terms or a timing mismatch in management account reporting.
Net working capital has significantly increased in 2025, largely driven by 'Amounts owed by connected companies' (£122,038.22) which may not be operationally liquid.
The business is a net consumer of working capital as it scales, with WC as % of revenue rising from 9% to 16.7%.
The asset base is exceptionally fresh (81% NBV/Cost) due to a major fleet renewal program in 2023-2024.
Vehicles represent 89.6% of the total Net Book Value.
Capex cliff risk is low; only the investment property and showroom fit-out are aged, but these are not critical to core service delivery.
Maintenance capex is expected to rise as the new fleet begins to age out of warranty periods.
Revenue per employee of £108k is healthy for the home services sector.
Significant investment in marketing and SEO (3 dedicated staff) suggests a focus on digital lead generation.
The use of 3 apprentices (16.6% of headcount) provides a cost-effective talent pipeline but requires senior oversight.
Payroll as % of revenue has decreased from 31% in FY2024 to 23% in 2025, indicating improved operating leverage.

owner_dependency.critical_function_concentration: The General Manager holds significant operational control, while the Director focuses on high-level strategy and likely sales.
observations: Low direct salary for the owner (£8,580) is offset by dividends, a common SME structure.
The General Manager is the highest-paid individual, suggesting a level of professional management is already in place.
Dependency is mitigated by a structured office team (FC, Coordinator, Marketing).

scalability.capex_needed_for_growth: Minimal immediate capex; the current vehicle fleet is under-utilised or recently expanded to accommodate growth.
bottlenecks: Availability of qualified Senior Engineers to lead apprentice-heavy teams.
Collection of trade debtors which has slowed in the most recent period.
observations: The business has already demonstrated scalability, growing revenue by 77% between 2022 and 2025.
The high proportion of fixed-cost marketing staff suggests that incremental revenue will have high contribution margins.
The modern fleet reduces the risk of operational downtime during a growth phase.

key_findings: Strong asset freshness (81%) following a 2023/24 fleet refresh.
Healthy revenue per employee and improving payroll efficiency.
Significant intercompany loan balance (£122k) impacting the current working capital profile.
Transition from a small owner-led business to a professionally managed operation is well underway.
red_flags: Debtor days increasing to 42.5 days with 32% of ledger in the 31-60 day bracket.
Significant 'Other Long Term Debt' of £319,252 in 2025 balance sheet requires clarification.
Negative Hire Purchase Long Term balance (-£167,914) in 2025 management accounts suggests a potential accounting misclassification.
narrative: Thor-CON exhibits strong operational fundamentals characterized by a modern, well-maintained asset base and a productive workforce. The company has successfully scaled revenue while improving its payroll-to-revenue ratio. While the working capital cycle has lengthened recently, this is partly due to non-operational intercompany balances. The business is well-positioned for further growth without immediate heavy capital requirements, provided it can stabilize its debtor collection and manage the transition of its apprentice-heavy engineering team into fully productive units.
